newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares rise but deals few.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares rise but deals few.

text.p: Shares of oil marketing companies climbed on the Nigerian stock exchange on Monday but only a very few were traded, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6,860.45 from 6,850.02 on Friday.
"Nobody is willing to sell oil marketing company shares despite incessant hikes in their prices. There has been no appreciable quantity sold by anyone," one said.
Agip was the biggest beneficiary, gaining 40 kobo to 20.60 naira. African Petroleum and National Oil rose 30 kobo each to 42.30 naira and 44.30 naira respectively.
Total hit 55.00 naira with a 15 kobo appreciation.
Gains by Nigerian Breweries and Guinness were modest after steep rises last week. Nigerian Breweries ended 10 kobo higher at 17.60 naira. Guinness added 20 kobo to 7.10 naira.
West African Portland Cement Company finished at 42.30 naira, up 10 kobo, but Ashaka Cement fell five kobo to 17.90 naira.
Guaranty Trust Bank closed down 10 kobo at 12.50 naira and Union Bank the same margin down at 5.40 naira.
CFAO dropped 10 kobo to 3.00 naira while UAC closed at 7.94 naira, down four kobo.
Afprint, a leading firm in the textiles sector, fell four kobo to 2.75 naira.

Overall trading volume was boosted by two transactions for some six million shares of Nigerian Textile Mills at 1.36 naira per share as part of an out of court settlement over a disagreement resulting from the last public issue five years ago.
